title: Turn 6: cast Edgar through the Incubator, or keep casting Vampires?

board.you: Turn 6, precombat main, 34 life, land drop already made. Battlefield: Urza's Incubator naming Vampire, Anointed Procession, Sanctum Seeker, Cruel Celebrant, Viscera Seer, three 1/1 black Vampire tokens banked by eminence (Celebrant, Seer and Seeker were the casts; Procession landed last turn and has doubled nothing yet), Arcane Signet, and five lands - Command Tower, Blood Crypt, Godless Shrine, Savai Triome, Swamp - all untapped. Six mana available, all three colours live. Edgar Markov is in the command zone and has never been cast; through the Incubator he costs {1}{R}{W}{B}.
board.table: Player 2 (Esper draw-go) is at 34 with five untapped lands and has put nothing on the battlefield since turn 3. Stated assumption: a control seat at this bracket that passes with four or more untapped lands is holding a sweeper or a counterspell. Player 3 (Gruul aggro) is at 14, tapped out, with a 4/4 and a 3/3; they spent last turn attacking Player 4. Player 4 (Simic ramp) is at 38 with two untapped lands and is drawing two extra cards a turn.

scenario.extras: Count what one Vampire cast makes on this board. Eminence mints one 1/1 black Vampire from the command zone; Anointed Procession replaces that with two. The Incubator takes up to {2} of GENERIC cost off a Vampire creature spell: Edgar {3}{R}{W}{B} to {1}{R}{W}{B}, Charismatic Conqueror {1}{W} to {W}, Cordial Vampire {B}{B} and Bloodghast {B}{B} untouched. Sanctum Seeker: each attacking Vampire is 1 life from each opponent and 1 to you - stack 003 counted seven attackers as seven triggers. Viscera Seer sacrifices for no mana; with Cruel Celebrant out each of your creatures' deaths is 1 from each opponent and 1 to you, and Cordial Vampire, once on the battlefield, adds a +1/+1 counter to each Vampire per death. Flawless Maneuver costs {2}{W} while Edgar is in the command zone and {0} once he is on the battlefield. Goldfish: Edgar is cast by turn six in 69.8% of games (mean 5.775, median 6); mean bodies by turn six is 4.343 and you have six. No loop half is on the battlefield or in hand: the kill - Bloodthirsty Conqueror with Vito, Sanguine Bond or Enduring Tenacity (stacks 004, 006, 012) - needs no Edgar.
scenario.question: Edgar costs four for the first time and the table has not yet seen what your board does. Cast Charismatic Conqueror and then Edgar and alpha-strike behind a free Flawless Maneuver, leave him in the zone and turn the same mana into three Vampire casts and six tokens, or cast two and hold Maneuver at full price?

branches.choice: Cast Charismatic Conqueror, then Edgar, and alpha-strike behind a free Flawless Maneuver
branches.line:
Conqueror first for {W}: eminence mints one 1/1 from the command zone and Procession makes it two. Then Edgar for {1}{R}{W}{B}. One mana left.

Attack with seven: Edgar, Sanctum Seeker, Cruel Celebrant, Viscera Seer and the three banked tokens. Conqueror and its two tokens stay home, summoning sick. Seven Seeker triggers: each opponent loses 7 and you gain 7 at declare attackers, before a blocker is named.

Edgar's attack trigger puts a +1/+1 counter on every Vampire you control, the sick ones included. Player 3 is at 7 facing 19 power - Edgar 5/5 first strike, Seeker 4/5, three 2/2 tokens, Celebrant 2/3, Seer 2/2 - and two blockers stop at most nine of it. They die.

Flawless Maneuver is free from the moment Edgar resolves. Cordial Vampire and Bloodghast stay in hand.
branches.signals:
Seven life off every seat at declare attackers is the loudest thing this board has done, and the table re-ranks you on the spot.

Player 2's five open lands are answered with a spell that now costs zero; you present lethal on one seat and hold the answer in the same breath.

Conqueror's tax goes live the moment he lands: every artifact or creature Player 4 ramps into either enters tapped or hands you a 1/1 lifelink Vampire - a life-gain event for any converter you draw later.

Two cards stay in hand, where no sweeper reaches them.
branches.coalition_risk:
High, and paid for. One seat leaves; the two that remain lost seven each and watched a commander with haste do it.

If Edgar eats the removal that follows, he goes back to the zone and his next cast carries {2} of tax - {3}{R}{W}{B} through the Incubator. Eminence keeps minting from the zone either way.

The sacrifice fallback is still on the table: Seer and Celebrant turn every body into one life from each seat in response to anything.
branches.coaching:
The Incubator changed the price, and the price is the decision. Edgar at six was the whole turn; Edgar at four rides beside a Vampire cast, so the mint still happens and the commander arrives with it.

He earns the cast on two counts at once. He closes: Player 3 dies to the counters and the drain with your board intact, no body fed to Seer. He protects: Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat are free with a commander on the battlefield and Akroma's Will takes both modes. The loop that ends games - Conqueror with Vito, Sanguine Bond or Tenacity, stacks 004, 006, 012 - never needs him, but its commit turn wants those answers held for nothing.

You are ahead - six bodies on turn six against a mean of 4.343 - and from ahead you hedge: deploy what you need, bank protection. Cordial and Bloodghast in hand are the rebuild if the sweeper comes.

Price Maneuver honestly. Indestructible answers destroy. Against -X/-X or exile the answer is Seer and Celebrant in response, one life from each seat per body.

citations.quote: An ability triggers only once each time its trigger event occurs. However, it can trigger repeatedly if one event contains multiple occurrences.
If a creature has haste, it can attack even if it hasn’t been controlled by its controller continuously since their most recent turn began.
A commander cast from the command zone costs an additional {2} for each previous time the player casting it has cast it from the command zone that game.
If a commander is in a graveyard or in exile and that object was put into that zone since the last time state-based actions were checked, its owner may put it into the command zone.
Make it a comparison, not a habit — cast it when the body closes or protects, else spend the mana on something nobody can tax
When ahead, hedging is correct: deploy only what you need, simplify, bank protection.

branches.choice: Leave Edgar in the zone and cast all three Vampires
branches.line:
Conqueror for {W}, Cordial for {B}{B}, Bloodghast for {B}{B}: five mana, three eminence events, six 1/1 black tokens through Procession, three bodies. One mana floats.

Attack with the six that can: Seeker, Celebrant, Seer and the three banked tokens. Six Seeker triggers: each opponent loses 6, you gain 6.

Player 3 is at 8 and blocks two attackers. After blocks, feed the four new tokens that could not attack anyway to Viscera Seer: four Celebrant triggers take 4 more from every seat, and four Cordial counters go on every Vampire you control. Player 3 is at 4 against four unblocked 5-power attackers. Dead.

The other seats are at 24. You keep Seeker, Celebrant, Seer, Conqueror, Cordial, Bloodghast and five tokens, every one +4/+4. Edgar is home. Maneuver costs three you do not have.
branches.signals:
Three two-drops read as a durdle for about four seconds, until the table counts six tokens. Bloodghast has haste only once an opponent is at 10 or less; Player 3 is at 14 when you declare, so he stays home.

Then they learn two things. Your engine makes bodies that come back - Bloodghast returns on every land drop. And a counterspell only shaves one cast: eminence triggers on the cast, and the trigger sits on the stack on its own, so countering Cordial still mints two tokens.

Ten life off every seat before the turn ends makes you the archenemy, with the damage already dealt - the good version of that job.
branches.coalition_risk:
Real, and mostly pre-paid. Player 3 dies without one point of combat damage reaching them through a blocker they could choose; nobody fogs a Celebrant trigger.

You pass tapped out with eleven creatures and no protection spell you can cast. What you have instead is the response that fits this deck: a sweeper on the stack is answered by sacrificing the whole board to Seer, eleven bodies, eleven life from every seat on the way out, and Bloodghast comes back on the next land. Name that out loud and accept the empty board after it.
branches.coaching:
This was the right branch on v1.1.0, when a converter on the battlefield turned every eminence mint into damage to each seat. It left the 99. On v2.1.0 a mint is a body, and a body is worth what an outlet and a drain make of it - here, one life from each seat through Celebrant.

So count what the branch buys over casting Edgar: three more life off each seat, four more tokens, Cordial and Bloodghast on the battlefield, four counters on everything. And what it costs: four bodies fed to Seer, a hand of one dead card, and Edgar a full turn later, which is a turn later for the free Maneuver and Swat.

The kill does not need him - the three verified loops run through Bloodthirsty Conqueror, not the commander. The commit turn does want him, because that is the turn the table's answers come out and yours should cost nothing.

Take this branch when the open mana across the table is a counterspell rather than a sweeper - a counter on a two-drop still mints - or when Cordial's counters are what make next turn lethal. The goldfish does not see Bloodghast's return, so no figure here prices it.

citations.quote: An ability that states which zones it functions in functions only from those zones.
Once activated or triggered, an ability exists on the stack independently of its source. Destruction or removal of the source after that time won’t affect the ability.
Effects that use the word “instead” are replacement effects.
A creature can’t attack unless it has been under its controller’s control continuously since their most recent turn began.
The term dies means “is put into a graveyard from the battlefield.”
a wrath on the stack is answered by sacrificing the whole board in response — each body a card, the drains firing on the way out
Your cards should do something to all three seats or win the game; anything else is someone else's job.

branches.choice: Cast Conqueror and Cordial, and hold three for a hard-cast Flawless Maneuver
branches.line:
Three mana: Conqueror for {W}, Cordial for {B}{B}. Two eminence events, four tokens through Procession. Three mana stays up for Maneuver at {2}{W}.

Attack with the same six: Seeker, Celebrant, Seer, three banked tokens. Six Seeker triggers, 6 from every seat, Player 3 to 8. After blocks, feed the four new tokens to Seer: 4 more from every seat through Celebrant, four Cordial counters on every Vampire. Player 3 is dead; the other seats are at 24.

You pass with Seeker, Celebrant, Seer, Conqueror, Cordial and three tokens, all +4/+4, Bloodghast in hand, indestructible held up, Edgar home.
branches.signals:
Passing with three untapped after two spells reads as protection held, and it is.

It also reads as a player who paid three mana to be afraid of a card they have not seen, and Player 2 learns that four open lands slow you down. That is a lesson you would rather they never got.
branches.coalition_risk:
The mildest of the three. Player 3 still dies, so the aggro clock comes off the table, and ten per seat is what branch two deals anyway.

The cost goes to Player 4. The Simic seat drawing two extra cards a turn wins long games, and this branch donates a turn of Edgar to the idea that games should be longer.
branches.coaching:
This is the disciplined-looking branch, and the Incubator made it the wrong one.

It pays three mana for Flawless Maneuver. One more mana casts Edgar, who makes Maneuver free, makes Deflecting Swat free, adds a 4/4 first-strike haste attacker and a counter on every Vampire, and takes seven per seat instead of six at declare attackers. You are paying three for a thing four would have bought with a commander attached.

Price the insurance too. Indestructible answers destroy. It does not answer -X/-X and it does not answer exile, and your own 99 runs Olivia's Wrath and Path to Exile, which tells you how common those are at this table. For those, the answer is the same in every branch: Seer and Celebrant in response.

Take this shape only when Edgar is not castable - the Incubator is not out, or he has been cast twice and the tax is real. Here he is four mana and the hold costs you him.

citations.quote: what you lose if the wrath comes now versus what holding a threat back costs in clock and position — and against a control deck, holding back often IS the loss, because buying time is exactly their plan
the engine's hub justifies constant protection down plus a held response on the pivot turn

recommendation.choice: Cast Charismatic Conqueror, then Edgar, and alpha-strike behind a free Flawless Maneuver
recommendation.rationale:
The arithmetic that kept Edgar home on v1.1.0 was nine damage a seat from an entry converter on three casts. That converter left the 99, and Urza's Incubator put the commander at four. Both halves of the old answer moved, and the answer moves with them.

Five mana now buys Conqueror and Edgar together: the mint happens, seven life leaves every seat at declare attackers, Player 3 dies to counters and a first-strike commander with your board intact, and Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat cost nothing from here on. Cordial Vampire and Bloodghast wait in hand, out of a sweeper's reach.

Branch two takes ten a seat instead of seven. It pays with four bodies fed to Seer, a hand of one spell you cannot cast, and a commander who arrives a turn later - the turn you would rather have the free answers already. From ahead, six bodies on turn six against a goldfish mean of 4.343, that is the wrong trade.

The kill is unchanged: Bloodthirsty Conqueror with Vito, Sanguine Bond or Enduring Tenacity, stacks 004, 006 and 012, none of which asks for Edgar. He is there so that the turn you assemble one, the table's answers meet a Swat that cost you nothing.

So: Conqueror first, so his two tokens are on the battlefield for the counter. Then Edgar. Then seven attackers, Maneuver held free, and one mana floating that you did not need.
